key_insight: Simple local quantum processes can match the statistics of random unitaries (form a t-design) while still being efficiently distinguishable from truly random circuits.
engineering_relevance: This warns that unitary design metrics alone may be insufficient to certify pseudorandomness or scrambling in quantum circuit design, benchmarking, and physics-inspired simulations.
method: Construct efficient families of 1- and 2-qubit gate distributions
Compose them for T=O_t(n^2 log^2 n) independent steps
Test distinguishability from Haar-random unitaries with efficient quantum algorithms
evidence_signal: The abstract reports approximate unitary t-design behavior with negligible error exp(-Ω(log^2 n)) while an efficient distinguisher succeeds using only O_t(log^2 n) queries.
watch_item: Results show that high moment matching can still hide exploitable structure, so design-based validation may overestimate pseudorandomness for practical quantum workloads.
paper_title: On the pseudorandomness of simple quantum processes
